question: How many Fundamental Duties are there for citizens of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4 (11)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** of Indian citizens are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution under Part IV-A.
 
• Initially, **10 Fundamental Duties** were introduced by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1976**, based on recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• An additional duty, making the total count **11 Fundamental Duties**, was added by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act** in **2002**. This amendment introduced the duty to provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable but serve as moral and civic obligations for citizens to ensure the promotion of harmony and the spirit of patriotism.
 
• These duties apply to all Indian citizens and provide a framework to ensure responsible behavior in society and towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of **USSR (Russia)** and are unique in their inclusion in the Indian Constitution.
 
• They emphasize **individual responsibility** and collective societal well-being.
 
• These duties are aligned with the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and aim to strengthen national integrity and unity.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Respect the **Constitution**, **National Flag**, and **National Anthem**.
 
• Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all people of India and renounce practices derogatory to women.
 
• Preserve the rich **heritage of India's culture**.
 
• Protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
 
• Develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• Safeguard public property and abjure violence.
 
• Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
• Provide opportunities for education to children between **6 and 14 years** (added by the 86th Amendment Act).
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments Related to Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act (1976)** introduced the concept of Fundamental Duties.
 
• The **86th Amendment Act (2002)** added the duty related to education for children.
 
 
 
• **Enforcement:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are **non-justiciable**, meaning citizens cannot be legally punished for their violation.
 
• However, they serve as a moral compass for citizens to contribute positively to society.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Fundamental Duties in Practice:**
 
 
• Participation in **national festivals**, respecting symbols like the National Flag and National Anthem.
 
• Promoting **environmental conservation** through tree planting drives and wildlife protection initiatives.
 
• Encouraging **scientific temper** by supporting innovation and education.
 
• Fostering gender equality and renouncing practices derogatory to women.
